paper_metadata.title: Effect of Annealing Temperatures on Phase Stability, Mechanical Properties, and High-Temperature Steam Corrosion Resistance of (FeNi)67Cr15Mn10Al5Ti3 Alloy

evidence.quote: The effect of different annealing temperatures on the phase stability and mechanical properties of (FeNi)67Cr15Mn10Al5Ti3 high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied.

evidence.section: 3.1. Analysis of Phase and Microstructure Evolution
evidence.quote: Figure 2a,b show that the as-cast (FeNi)67Cr15Mn10Al5Ti3 exhibited a typical dendrite structure, consisting of uneven black dendrite structures (DR) and interdendrite structures (ID).

evidence.section: 3.1. Analysis of Phase and Microstructure Evolution
evidence.quote: According to Figure 2b, the ID structure was loose, and there were interdendrite gaps.

evidence.section: 3.1. Analysis of Phase and Microstructure Evolution
evidence.quote: The Al and Ti of the as-cast sample segregated at the ID for different radii, valence electron concentrations, and electronegativities.

evidence.section: 3.1. Analysis of Phase and Microstructure Evolution
evidence.quote: The average grain size was 13.2 µm, and a clear grain boundary was seen when the HEA was annealed at 800 ◦C.

evidence.section: 3.1. Analysis of Phase and Microstructure Evolution
evidence.quote: At 1000 ◦C, the crystal grain size was relatively uniform, the crystal grains became round, and the average crystal grain size was about 23.8µm.
The hardness of the alloy declined from 327.72 HV for the as-cast condition to 240.33 HV at 900 ◦C, decreasing by about 26.7%.
The hardness of the alloy declined from 327.72 HV for the as-cast condition to 240.33 HV at 900 ◦C, decreasing by about 26.7%.
At 1000 ◦C, the hardness decreased by 10.4% compared with that of the as-cast alloy.
When exposed to an annealing temperature of less than 800 ◦C, the solid solution structure homogenized, and grain coarsening led to a decrease in hardness [35].
The decline in yield strength and the increase in tensile elongation were caused by homogenization of the single solid solution and coarsening of the grain size.

evidence.section: 3.1. Analysis of Phase and Microstructure Evolution
evidence.quote: At a low annealing temperature (≤800 ◦C), the elements of (FeNi)67Cr15Mn10Al5Ti3 HEA diffused through the grain boundary, and the solid solution became larger and precipitated out.

evidence.section: 3.1. Analysis of Phase and Microstructure Evolution
evidence.quote: At a higher annealing temperature (>800 ◦C), the mixing entropy of the alloying elements increased, diffusion at grain boundaries was suppressed, and the unevenly distributed elements presented with a uniform grain size.
